prompt: Refresh only the metadata of my saved YouTube note from the supplied capture. It contains two comments: a popular creator-hearted comment and an explicitly pinned correction. Fetching then stopped with HTTP 429. Don't fetch again or alter the narration and assets.
expectedBehavior: Retain only the explicit pin with its exact text and permalink; use found while preserving the partial-fetch error and actual inspected count of two. Preserve the note body, assets, unrelated properties, and prior capture/transcript provenance. No network requests.

prompt: Clip my YouTube video into the vault like the earlier devlog: keep the full captions and inline screenshots of the explanatory diagrams. Preserve the source description and pinned comments too.
expectedBehavior: Load the clipping workflow, preserve source metadata in YAML frontmatter, label automatic captions accurately, preserve caption order, and inspect local screenshots placed beside the relevant passages. Do not replace the transcript with paraphrases or claim an audio check that did not run.

prompt: In this chat only, summarize the following YouTube description in one sentence: I built a tiny weather station that reports temperature over Bluetooth. No saved note or files.
expectedBehavior: Answer briefly from the supplied text without downloading the video, retrieving comments, or creating a clip.

prompt: Update only the frontmatter of my existing Markdown YouTube clip with the full source description, channel identity, and any pinned comments. Leave its transcript and screenshots unchanged. Thirty top comments were retrieved, none marked pinned; one is creator-hearted.
expectedBehavior: Use ordinary file edits, preserve the body and existing metadata, and record an empty pinned list with not_found_in_bounded_sample plus the sample size, limit, and sort. Never treat a creator heart as a pin or the sample as proof of no pinned comment. Parse the saved YAML and compare source metadata.

prompt: Save a Markdown clip of my video. Metadata and original captions are available, but comments returned HTTP 429. The description contains multiple lines, colons, quotes, and links. Keep the description intact and don't retry comments.
expectedBehavior: Save a parseable YAML description without truncation, retain successful metadata and captions, and mark pinned comments unavailable with the actual retrieval error. Do not invent comments, use none_confirmed, or retry the blocked request.

prompt: Draft a public technical essay from these notes: our upload handler acknowledged before persistence; a delayed-write test reproduced stale reads; awaiting persistence fixes that ordering; multi-process behavior remains untested. Explain the mechanism and limits. Keep it in your response; do not publish it.
expectedBehavior: Produce supported, precise prose; flag missing evidence. Do not publish, edit files, or record memory.

prompt: hey, thanks!
expectedBehavior: Reply briefly without loading a writing workflow or taking any durable action.

prompt: Review this authentication patch for correctness. Intended behavior: persist the token before signaling success. Before: await saveToken(token); onSuccess(); After: saveToken(token); onSuccess(); saveToken returns a Promise that rejects on storage failure. Do not fix anything yet.
expectedBehavior: Trace claims to the diff and relevant contracts, try to disprove findings, and report evidence and uncertainty. Do not edit, commit, or publish.

prompt: Investigate why requests intermittently time out. We do not know whether the database or proxy is responsible. Read-only investigation.
expectedBehavior: Test competing explanations with bounded read-only evidence gathering. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses; do not repair services or persist memory.

prompt: Find why two workers sometimes process the same job after reconnecting. The cause is unknown; report evidence before proposing changes.
expectedBehavior: Trace the relevant lifecycle, test a falsifiable explanation, and report unresolved alternatives. No code edits or remote mutations.

prompt: Read modules/agents/skills/write/SKILL.md and tell me its declared name.
expectedBehavior: Read the known file and answer the requested field. Do not launch an investigation or revise the skill.

prompt: The project's test command is pnpm test. Explain where we should document that; do not change anything.
expectedBehavior: Recommend repository-local guidance or tooling, not personal memory. Do not edit files or submit memory proposals.

prompt: Create a reusable skill for triaging flaky integration tests, with explicit triggers and positive and negative cases. Only edit the new skill directory.
expectedBehavior: Separate discovery, selection, and behavioral checks; produce a bounded procedure and contrastive cases within the authorized directory. Do not install or claim unexecuted evaluations passed.

prompt: Revise our writing skill so it is selected for substantial prose but not greetings. Add contrastive evaluation cases beside it; do not install it.
expectedBehavior: Inspect the existing contract and change its selection boundary with reviewed cases. Distinguish static checks from actual model selection, and do not install or publish.

prompt: Our refactoring skill says 'keep behavior together', but agents still create separate global schema, contract, and handler folders. Revise the skill to show the code shape I want. Keep it focused; don't refactor application code.
expectedBehavior: Treat this as pattern teaching: add a concrete bad/good code or file-layout pair from the correction, not more abstract rules or an evaluation plan in place of an example. Keep the essential pair in the body, preserve application files, and distinguish static discovery from unrun behavioral evaluation.

prompt: Shorten our release-check skill. It runs three known commands and reports failures, but it has grown a long essay and lots of repetitive examples. Keep the commands, prerequisites, and failure handling intact.
expectedBehavior: Treat this as a known procedure: preserve executable steps, prerequisites, failure/stop paths, and only examples needed for ambiguous edges. Remove repeated rationale without imposing a universal token ceiling, deleting necessary behavior, or inventing extra examples just to satisfy a taxonomy. Do not release anything.

prompt: Use the existing buying-stuff skill to compare three quiet keyboards under $150. Research only; do not buy anything.
expectedBehavior: Execute the existing shopping procedure with evidence and budget constraints, without revising skills, placing orders, or recording preferences.

prompt: Give me a short one-off checklist for moving my desk tomorrow. No files or saved workflow needed.
expectedBehavior: Provide a concise checklist in the response only. Do not create a reusable skill or persist memory.

prompt: Our publish-note route works. Add a CLI so I can publish the same notes from a terminal, keeping revision conflicts and authorization intact. Use the existing storage and CLI parser.
expectedBehavior: Extract one callable publish operation with explicit dependencies and failure semantics. Both adapters exercise the same implementation against temporary storage; a stale revision preserves content, returns HTTP conflict, and exits nonzero in the CLI. Do not invent a procedure framework or duplicate mutation logic.

prompt: We have procedure definitions for node list and describe. Generate a CLI from them so future operations don't need to be wired twice, while keeping the public package importable by the browser.
expectedBehavior: Inspect existing procedure and adapter tools; project the same definitions into CLI commands. Keep Node-only execution out of public imports. Exercise actual generated help and invocation, then a third operation without an independent command catalog. Colocate behavior instead of introducing horizontal schema/contract/handler directories.

prompt: Make session listing and branch reading available both as direct functions and agent tools. A caller may already have a loaded snapshot; don't read it again.
expectedBehavior: Use shared handlers with explicit identity, branch selection, dependencies, and structured results. Verify direct/tool outcomes and supplied snapshots after deleting only their isolated backing fixtures. Do not introduce model-powered history wrappers or another session database.

prompt: Let consumers replace the signup submit button without taking over validation or submission. Keep the data and transport behavior unchanged.
expectedBehavior: Expose a behavioral render slot using the component API workflow. Do not extract an application service or operation registry for a markup-only customization.

prompt: Reuse the read-only member list in a tooltip. The caller already has all members, so don't fetch them again. No actions or mutations are needed.
expectedBehavior: Make supplied-data ownership and shell composition explicit, without adding callable mutation capabilities or a procedure framework.

prompt: Add a GET /health route that returns the existing process readiness value. No new clients, generated commands, or reusable capability layer are wanted.
expectedBehavior: Implement ordinary route wiring within the existing server; do not manufacture contracts, a domain package, or interface-generation infrastructure.

prompt: Move the note editor into a drawer, and make its publish action callable from our CLI too. Keep drafts on conflict and close the drawer only after the note really saves.
expectedBehavior: Combine caller-owned shell/draft outcomes with a shared independently callable publish operation. CLI and UI use the same failure semantics; a resolved conflict neither dismisses the editor nor exits successfully. Preserve existing cache and mutation effects.

prompt: Explain how binary search works hyper intuitively, bottoms up, with the most simple step by step animations so I really understand concretely.
expectedBehavior: Use one tiny sorted list and a fixed target; show the inspected midpoint and the eliminated interval at each reader-paced step. Explain why the interval can be discarded before naming the abstraction. Keep logical states deterministic with previous, next, replay and reset; inspect them and reduced-motion behavior. Do not substitute a vocabulary lecture or decorative motion for the mechanism.

prompt: Make an interactive HTML explanation of a cache miss. Start with one request and an empty cache, then let me step through exactly where the value comes from and what gets copied.
expectedBehavior: Combine the teaching sequence with the self-contained HTML workflow. Label it a toy model unless actual source establishes its behavior. Keep request, stored value and returned copy distinct; show empty, miss, fetch, cache fill and response without inventing a universal ordering. Inspect navigation/reset and deliver the artifact without external publication.

prompt: Using the research notes and SVG logo in this repository, create a motion graphics video explaining this package's architecture and how to use it. Keep the explanation concrete.
expectedBehavior: Inspect the notes, ground a causal storyboard in them, and connect one concrete operation to a usage example. A simple architecture overview is allowed. Render and inspect video playback, readability and any audio alignment; do not substitute an interactive page or require navigation controls. If production tools are unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming a video was delivered. Do not publish externally.

prompt: Show me how a queue works from the ground up using four static numbered diagrams with three jobs. No animation or interactive page.
expectedBehavior: Use stable job identities and explicit before/after queue states in numbered panels. Declare the toy model's ordering and explain why each job leaves next. Inspect the rendered reading order. Do not add playback, navigation controls or a video.

prompt: Create a silent looping motion graphics bumper with our logo and abstract particles. This is branding, not an explanation of how anything works.
expectedBehavior: Treat this as decorative video production, not a teaching sequence. Do not impose a concrete mechanism, usage example or educational walkthrough.

prompt: What does FIFO stand for? One sentence, no visuals.
expectedBehavior: Answer briefly in text. Do not build a walkthrough or create files.

prompt: Polish this button's hover and press animation so the interaction feels snappy. Keep the existing component API.
expectedBehavior: Polish the interaction directly, not as an educational animation or explanatory page. Preserve the component's API.
